items.title: 1. Site visit and analysis
items.text: The initial stage, at which the basis of the future project is formed. I go to the site, assess the relief, existing plantings, lighting, engineering conditions and architecture of the building. This allows us to understand the potential of the space and determine the optimal direction of the future design.

items.title: 2. Concept formation
items.text: At this stage, a general idea of ​​the space is created. The style, functional zoning, scenarios for using the site and the mood of the future garden are determined. The concept is the foundation that combines aesthetics and practicality.

items.title: 3. Planning solution (2D)
items.text: A detailed plan of the site is developed with all the main elements: paths, terraces, recreation areas, landscaping and other objects. It is at this stage that the structure of the space is agreed upon before moving on to visualization.

items.title: 4. Project visualization
items.text: Realistic images of the future space are created, allowing you to see what the site will look like before work begins. This makes it possible to make adjustments and achieve the ideal result even at the design stage.

items.title: 5. Working documentation
items.text: After approval of the visual part, a full set of drawings is developed for the implementation of the project. It includes all the necessary technical solutions for construction, landscaping and engineering systems.

items.title: 6. Project Album
items.text: The final stage is the formation of a complete project album. You receive a structured document that contains: • visualizations • drawings • all necessary materials for implementation This is a clear instruction that allows you to implement the project without losing quality and ideas.

details.heading: Site visit for assessment and familiarization
details.text: This is the first and very important step. On site, we assess the features of the plot: shape, terrain, sunlight exposure, and any existing plants or structures. During the visit we take notes, mark key points, and identify the best solutions for the functionality and aesthetics of the space.

details.heading: 2D sketch plan of the site
details.text: After the site visit, a complete 2D sketch plan is created. It shows the layout of paths, green zones with plants, key elements of the space, and areas for rest or activities. The plan accounts for the site's ergonomics — how convenient it is to move through and use the space.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Answers to what clients ask us most often

items.question: What is the difference between the "Architectural Base", "Project Plus" and "Premium" packages?
items.answer: "Architectural Base" includes only technical drawings without visualization — a technical foundation without visuals. "Project Plus" is a full project with 2D planning, simplified technical drawings, visualizations and a materials album. "Premium" is the most detailed package: everything from "Project Plus" plus full detailed technical drawings and a rendered video of the space.

items.question: How long does it take to create a project?
items.answer: It depends on the scope of work and the size of the site. Approximate timeframes: space concept — 7–14 days, visualization — 14–21 days, architectural base — 14–21 days, "Project Plus" — 21–42 days, "Premium" — 30–60 days.

items.question: What stages does a project go through, from concept to the finished album?
items.answer: 1. Discussing ideas and concept. 2. Developing the 2D concept with room for revisions. 3. 3D visualization — day and night renders. 4. Developing technical drawings. 5. Delivering the album: first a digital PDF, then the printed album.

items.question: Does it include a consultation on choosing plants and materials?
items.answer: Yes, it's part of the concept development process. At this stage we take all of the client's preferences into account and discuss stylistic and functional decisions, so every element fits the project harmoniously.

items.question: What needs to be prepared before the work begins?
items.answer: It's essential to commission a professional geodetic survey of the site. The accuracy of these measurements determines all further planning, the concept and the technical drawings.

items.question: Are revisions included in the project price?
items.answer: All revisions during the concept stage are included in the price. Once the concept is approved, revisions to the visualizations are possible once — the client submits all requests together. Each further round of revisions costs $100.

items.question: Do you support the implementation of the project?
items.answer: Yes. We don't carry out the construction work ourselves, but we monitor key milestones, check that everything matches the project decisions, and provide consultations if you have questions during implementation.

items.question: Can the payment be split into stages?
items.answer: Yes: 50% before the work begins, during the site visit, and 50% upon delivery of the project. For large sites (50 sotok or more), payment for the "Project Plus" and "Premium" packages can be split into four stages of 25% each.

items.question: What format does the client receive after the project is finished?
items.answer: For the "Space Concept", "Space Visualization" and "Architectural Base" packages — a digital PDF file. For the "Project Plus" and "Premium" packages — a printed architectural album with all drawings, plans and visualizations.
